brief_scope: Portable local-workspace backup and preview-first restore for records, attachments, preferences, passphrase option, old/new schemas, interruption, removable media, merge, integrity and usability distinctions.

sources.title: SQLite Online Backup API and sqlite3_backup C interface
sources.released_version_or_commit: Live official SQLite C interface documentation; unversioned. Consulted 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Online Backup API; backup_init/step/finish; locking, retry, fatal error and destination-handle sections; lines 37-81 in the inspected page.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official API documentation and inspected copy consistency, lock duration, SQLITE_BUSY/LOCKED handling, fatal IOERR/NOMEM/READONLY handling, finish/rollback, concurrent source writes, and destination connection constraints.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Consistent point-in-time destination on successful completion; source read locks occur per step and external writes can restart the operation. BUSY/LOCKED can be retried; IOERR/NOMEM/READONLY are fatal. Destination connection must not be used by any API between init and finish.
sources.applicability: Conditional if the chosen engine is SQLite. Provides a safe database snapshot primitive, not a snapshot of attachments or preferences outside that database.

sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging documentation and WAL-reset bug notice
sources.released_version_or_commit: Live official SQLite documentation; unversioned. Bug notice names releases 3.7.0 through 3.51.2 and fixed releases 3.51.3+, 3.44.6, and 3.50.7.
sources.locator: Section 4 The WAL File; read-only conditions at lines 146-150; section 11 The WAL-Reset Bug at lines 191-196.
sources.observed_operation: Opened and inspected SQLite's WAL persistence requirements and current official bug/fix notice.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A live WAL database state spans main DB and -wal; separating them may lose committed transactions or corrupt the copy. -shm is coordination state and may be recreated. WAL-reset bug has a narrow concurrent-connection write/checkpoint condition; fixed in named releases.
sources.applicability: Conditional on SQLite/WAL use. Raw main-file copy is unsuitable for a live WAL database. The WAL-reset bug is a bundled-engine/version and concurrent-use qualification, not a claim that backup itself triggers it.

sources.title: SQLite PRAGMA reference and ALTER TABLE compatibility documentation
sources.released_version_or_commit: Live official SQLite reference; unversioned. Individual sections identify version additions/defaults.
sources.locator: PRAGMA user_version (lines 933-941); foreign_key_check (366-372); integrity_check (492-513); foreign_keys (383 onward, including historical default); journal_mode section (515 onward). Companion: https://sqlite.org/lang_altertable.html, compatibility history for 3.25.0/3.26.0 and safe rebuild guidance.
sources.observed_operation: Inspected exact descriptions and exclusions of SQLite's app-version, integrity, and foreign-key facilities, plus migration-sensitive ALTER TABLE behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: user_version is an app-owned integer that SQLite does not interpret. integrity_check does not find FK errors; foreign_key_check is separate. FK enforcement historically defaulted OFF as of 3.6.19, may be compile-time overridden, and may change in future. ALTER TABLE rename behavior changed in 3.25/3.26 and legacy mode changes behavior.
sources.applicability: Conditional if SQLite is selected; proves checks and metadata boundaries but not application-level validity or attachment integrity.

sources.title: Python 3.15 zipfile library documentation
sources.released_version_or_commit: Python 3.15.0 documentation edition; page also displays some API changes by version.
sources.locator: ZipFile.testzip() lines 231-236; member naming/encoding lines 240-252; Path path-sanitization warning at lines 298 onward.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official Python library docs and inspected archive CRC/header verification, path APIs, encoding notes, and member-name behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: testzip reads members and checks CRCs and headers, returning first bad filename or None. zipfile.Path does not sanitize untrusted names; the caller must validate. ZIP names are relative by convention; UTF-8 is written for non-ASCII, and a NUL in a filename is truncated by the module.
sources.applicability: Primary implementation documentation for ZIP verification/path handling behavior; design lesson applies to any extractor, but this is not a requirement to use Python.

sources.title: GHSA-94vh-gphv-8pm8 — Rust zip archive extraction symlink escape
sources.released_version_or_commit: Published 2025-03-16; affected zip crate versions >=1.3.0; patched 2.3.0.
sources.locator: Summary and details lines 131-161: earlier symlink entry could redirect later extraction outside target despite enclosed-name sanitization wording.
sources.observed_operation: Read the public security advisory and recorded affected range, path condition, impact, and fixed release.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Malicious archive can place a symlink to a parent before a later file; extraction did not validate final canonicalized path. Advisory says fixed in 2.3.0.
sources.applicability: Directly relevant if using the Rust zip crate or analogous sequential symlink extraction. Otherwise a public repair-history case supporting explicit path and symlink regression tests.

sources.title: age file encryption format, version 1.0.0
sources.released_version_or_commit: age format specification v1.0.0 (C2SP versioned specification).
sources.locator: Payload chunking/authentication lines 90-95; native recipients lines 96-99; scrypt stanza and AEAD lines 157-181.
sources.observed_operation: Read the pinned-format specification for passphrase key wrapping, authenticated streaming, final-chunk errors, recipient constraints, and work-factor requirements.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Passphrase is processed with scrypt and ChaCha20-Poly1305. Payload uses authenticated 64-KiB chunks; streaming decrypt must error without a valid final chunk. An scrypt stanza must be the only header stanza; implementation should cap work factor. The spec defines no account/service recovery mechanism.
sources.applicability: Candidate outer encryption envelope for a completed archive, if selected after implementation/runtime/interop review. It does not implement archive selection or app restore validation.

sources.title: restic 0.19.1 backup and repository checking documentation
sources.released_version_or_commit: restic documentation release 0.19.1; companion repository-check page https://restic.readthedocs.io/en/stable/045_working_with_repos.html.
sources.locator: Backup snapshots/dedup/check lines 65-116 and source read errors line 460; repository structural versus full data checks and --read-data lines 247-301.
sources.observed_operation: Read official restic docs to compare snapshot/dedup model, read-error semantics, repository requirements, and differing levels of integrity check.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Repeated backup uses dedup against a parent but creates logical snapshots. Read errors may coexist with a created snapshot. Default check validates repository structure; --read-data verifies stored pack contents at higher I/O/time cost.
sources.applicability: Alternative local repository strategy for space-efficient history; not a self-contained single archive and not a substitute for domain-aware preview, app migrations, or coordinated workspace snapshot.

sources.title: Rust std::fs::rename documentation
sources.released_version_or_commit: Stable Rust standard-library docs identify std 1.99.0 / source commit b940084d7 (2026-09-28) on the inspected module page; rename API is stable since 1.0.0.
sources.locator: Function overview and platform-specific behavior lines 21-44.
sources.observed_operation: Inspected rename replacement, cross-mount failure, and Unix/Windows distinctions in the standard library contract.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Rename replaces existing target where supported but fails across mount points; replacement of existing directories differs across Unix and Windows/filesystem capability.
sources.applicability: Conditional if Rust std::fs is used, and generally relevant to same-volume staged publication. It does not establish power-loss durability or atomic replacement of a multi-file workspace.

sources.title: NIST Secure Hash Standard FIPS 180-4, Update 1 final
sources.released_version_or_commit: FIPS 180-4 final updated specification, published 2015-08-04; NIST planning note says revision is planned after public comments (2023-03-07).
sources.locator: Abstract and document history; SHA-256 digest algorithm specified in FIPS 180-4.
sources.observed_operation: Opened NIST publication metadata and the linked FIPS document to confirm SHA-256's standardized message-digest purpose.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: FIPS 180-4 specifies hash digests used to detect message changes; a standalone digest does not authenticate who supplied data if the digest can be replaced with the data.
sources.applicability: Candidate manifest digest for detecting payload changes; pair with a trusted/authenticated manifest or AEAD where adversarial modification matters.
